category_specific_evidence: Issue #24073: jnp.polyfit with cov=True and full=False returns a covariance matrix C of shape (n, n, 1) regardless of y's shape, whereas numpy.polyfit returns one covariance matrix per right-hand side (e.g., 3 for num_rhs=3).

Root cause per PR #24074: taking fac = fac[0] from resids kept only the first rhs residual, so only the first set of coefficients received a covariance matrix; the fix moves the scalar conversion into the single-rhs branch and broadcasts fac over the rhs axis.

Patch in jax/_src/numpy/polynomial.py: for 1D y, fac = atleast_1d(fac)[np.newaxis] and returns Vbase * fac; for multi-rhs, returns Vbase[:, :, np.newaxis] * atleast_1d(fac)[np.newaxis, np.newaxis, :].
Test change in tests/lax_numpy_test.py testPolyfit adds num_rhs=[1, 5] parameter so multiple right-hand sides are exercised; tests use tol_spec {float32: 1e-3, float64: 1e-13, complex64: 1e-5}.
Patch adds ValueError when the number of data points does not exceed order when scaling the covariance matrix.
reproduction_risks: The issue example uses x = np.arange(10) cast to float32 with np.random.seed(1); the JAX output discrepancy from numpy is in the tiny numeric digits, so a reproduction comparing values should use a tolerance consistent with float32 and not exact equality.
The 1D and multi-rhs branches are handled differently in the fix, so a reproduction should test both y of shape (N,) and y of shape (N, num_rhs).
Tolerance value applied to the fixed test is only given as the test's tol_spec for float32 (1e-3); no explicit tolerance for this bug's reproduction is stated in the passages.
